title: Sim Lab Baseball Lab

steps.title: Make a curved ramp
steps.goal: Build a channel that keeps the ball on its path.
actions: Add two half cylinders. Make one slightly narrower than the other, but long enough to cut through both ends.
Set the smaller shape to Hole. Align it inside the solid shape to leave a curved wall.
Select both shapes and Group them. Keep the ball separate from the ramp.
Add a ball that fits inside the channel and a bat. Use the author’s video or copy the tutorial model if you need the starting shapes.
steps.check: The ramp is a hollow channel, and the ball fits inside it.
steps.caption: Original KIDSPRO construction screenshot (Japanese interface). The English instructions explain how to make the hollow channel.

steps.title: Tilt the ramp by 22.5°
steps.goal: Find the space the ramp needs to move.
actions: Select the ramp and use its rotation handle.
Rotate it 22.5° clockwise, as shown in the picture.
steps.check: The ramp is tilted by 22.5°.
steps.caption: English teaching image adapted from KIDSPRO’s screenshot. Click to enlarge.

steps.title: Set the bottom height to 0
steps.goal: Keep the tilted ramp above the workplane.
actions: With the ramp still tilted, use the lift handle.
Move it up until the bottom height reads 0.
steps.check: The lowest part touches the workplane instead of passing through it.
steps.caption: English teaching image adapted from KIDSPRO’s screenshot. Click to enlarge.

steps.title: Return the ramp to horizontal
steps.goal: Keep the clearance you just created.
actions: Rotate the ramp back to horizontal.
Keep its vertical position unchanged. Do not drop it onto the workplane.
steps.check: The ramp is horizontal and raised above the workplane.
steps.caption: English teaching image adapted from KIDSPRO’s screenshot. Click to enlarge.

steps.title: Open the Sim Lab shapes
steps.goal: Find the connectors that make shapes move.
actions: Open the Basic Shapes menu.
Choose Sim Lab from the shape categories.
steps.check: You can see the Sim Lab connectors.
steps.caption: English teaching image adapted from KIDSPRO’s screenshot. Click to enlarge.

steps.title: Add the ramp connector
steps.goal: Use an Axis Connector for turning movement.
actions: Drag an Axis Connector onto the workplane near the ramp.
steps.check: The connector is beside the ramp.
steps.caption: English teaching image adapted from KIDSPRO’s screenshot. Click to enlarge.

steps.title: Drag a Joint Point
steps.goal: Attach the connector to the shape it will move.
actions: Select the connector. Find one of its Joint Points.
Drag that Joint Point towards the ramp.
steps.check: The Joint Point reaches the ramp.
steps.caption: English teaching image adapted from KIDSPRO’s screenshot. Click to enlarge.

steps.title: Finish the connection
steps.goal: One connected end lets the ramp turn around a fixed axis.
actions: Drop the Joint Point onto the ramp.
Leave the other Joint Point unattached, as in the picture.
steps.check: The ramp is connected to the Axis Connector.
steps.caption: English teaching image adapted from KIDSPRO’s screenshot. Click to enlarge.

steps.title: Turn the connector by 90°
steps.goal: The connector direction controls the turning direction.
actions: Select the Axis Connector.
Rotate it 90° clockwise, matching the picture.
steps.check: The connector axis runs across the ramp, so the ramp can tilt.
steps.caption: English teaching image adapted from KIDSPRO’s screenshot. Click to enlarge.

steps.title: Align the ramp pivot
steps.goal: Place the connector at the middle of the ramp’s right side.
actions: Select the ramp and its connector. Open Align.
Use the alignment handles to position the connector as shown.
steps.check: The connector sits at the centre of the ramp’s right side.
steps.caption: English teaching image adapted from KIDSPRO’s screenshot. Click to enlarge.

steps.title: Open Motor Type
steps.goal: Select the connector, rather than the ramp itself.
actions: Click the ramp’s Axis Connector.
Find Motor Type in its settings and open the menu.
steps.check: The connector’s motor settings are visible.
steps.caption: English teaching image adapted from KIDSPRO’s screenshot. Click to enlarge.

steps.title: Choose Servo
steps.goal: A servo moves to a target angle.
actions: Set Motor Type to Servo.
Check the limits and torque against the settings below.
steps.check: Motor Type shows Servo.
steps.caption: English teaching image adapted from KIDSPRO’s screenshot. Click to enlarge.

steps.title: Slow the ramp down
steps.goal: Use a slow tilt so you can watch the ball move.
actions: Find Maximum Speed.
Enter 20 RPM and confirm the value.
steps.check: Maximum Speed is 20 RPM.
steps.caption: English teaching image adapted from KIDSPRO’s screenshot. Click to enlarge.

steps.title: Edit the ramp interaction
steps.goal: Connect a keyboard key to the motor.
actions: Keep the ramp connector selected.
Click Edit Interaction.
steps.check: The interaction keyboard is open.
steps.caption: English teaching image adapted from KIDSPRO’s screenshot. Click to enlarge.

steps.title: Choose key 1
steps.goal: Use the same key later to prepare the bat.
actions: Select the 1 key on the interaction keyboard.
steps.check: Key 1 is selected.
steps.caption: English teaching image adapted from KIDSPRO’s screenshot. Click to enlarge.

steps.title: Choose Set Position
steps.goal: Use an exact target angle.
actions: Open the action menu for key 1.
Choose Set Position.
steps.check: The action is Set Position, not Change Position.
steps.caption: English teaching image adapted from KIDSPRO’s screenshot. Click to enlarge.

steps.title: Set the ramp angle to 22.5°
steps.goal: Pressing 1 will tilt the ramp.
actions: Enter 22.5 for the target position and confirm.
Put the ball in the channel. Open Sim Lab and start the simulation.
Press 1. Check that the ramp tilts and the ball rolls.
Reset the simulation and return to design mode before continuing.
steps.check: The ramp tilts by 22.5° and releases the ball.
steps.caption: English teaching image adapted from KIDSPRO’s screenshot. Click to enlarge.

steps.title: Add the bat connector
steps.goal: The bat needs its own turning motor.
actions: Place a second Axis Connector on the workplane near the bat.
steps.check: There is one connector for the ramp and another for the bat.
steps.caption: English teaching image adapted from KIDSPRO’s screenshot. Click to enlarge.

steps.title: Place the bat pivot
steps.goal: The bat should turn around its handle end.
actions: Select the bat and its connector. Use Align.
Place the connector at the end of the bat, as shown.
steps.check: The pivot is at the handle end, not the middle of the bat.
steps.caption: English teaching image adapted from KIDSPRO’s screenshot. Click to enlarge.

steps.title: Connect the bat
steps.goal: Attach the moving shape to its connector.
actions: Drag one Joint Point onto the bat.
Leave the other Joint Point unattached.
steps.check: The connector is attached to the bat.
steps.caption: English teaching image adapted from KIDSPRO’s screenshot. Click to enlarge.

steps.title: Use a servo for the bat
steps.goal: Make the bat move between two set angles.
actions: Select the bat’s Axis Connector.
Set Motor Type to Servo.
steps.check: The bat connector shows Servo.
steps.caption: English teaching image adapted from KIDSPRO’s screenshot. Click to enlarge.

steps.title: Set the bat motor values
steps.goal: Give the bat enough turning force and speed.
actions: Set Motor Torque to 1000 N·m.
Keep Maximum Speed at 400 RPM.
Check that the lower limit is 0° and the upper limit is 180°.
steps.check: The values match the table below.
steps.tip: Torque is turning force. Maximum Speed tells you how fast the motor can turn. RPM means revolutions per minute.
steps.caption: English teaching image adapted from KIDSPRO’s screenshot. Click to enlarge.

steps.title: Edit the bat interaction
steps.goal: Choose what the bat does when you press a key.
actions: Keep the bat connector selected.
Click Edit Interaction.
steps.check: You are editing the bat connector, not the ramp connector.
steps.caption: English teaching image adapted from KIDSPRO’s screenshot. Click to enlarge.

steps.title: Choose key 1 for the bat
steps.goal: One key can control both connectors.
actions: Select 1 on the interaction keyboard.
steps.check: Key 1 is selected for the bat connector.
steps.caption: English teaching image adapted from KIDSPRO’s screenshot. Click to enlarge.

steps.title: Choose the bat’s first action
steps.goal: Send the bat to a target angle.
actions: Choose Set Position for key 1.
steps.check: The action is Set Position.
steps.caption: English teaching image adapted from KIDSPRO’s screenshot. Click to enlarge.

steps.title: Set the bat to 180°
steps.goal: This is the bat’s ready position.
actions: Enter 180 for the target position and confirm.
steps.check: Key 1 sends the bat to 180°.
steps.caption: English teaching image adapted from KIDSPRO’s screenshot. Click to enlarge.

steps.title: Choose key 2
steps.goal: Use another key to hit the ball.
actions: Select 2 on the interaction keyboard.
steps.check: Key 2 is selected for the bat connector.
steps.caption: English teaching image adapted from KIDSPRO’s screenshot. Click to enlarge.

steps.title: Choose Set Position again
steps.goal: The hitting motion returns the bat to its starting angle.
actions: Choose Set Position for key 2.
steps.check: Key 2 also uses Set Position.
steps.caption: English teaching image adapted from KIDSPRO’s screenshot. Click to enlarge.

steps.title: Return the bat to 0°
steps.goal: The bat swings back when you press 2.
actions: Enter 0 for key 2’s target position and confirm.
steps.caption: English teaching image adapted from KIDSPRO’s screenshot. Click to enlarge.

steps.title: Start the baseball simulation
steps.goal: Test the two connectors together.
actions: Position the ball in the ramp. Keep the ball, ramp and bat as separate objects.
Click Sim Lab at the top right.
Click the Start button at the lower left.
steps.check: The simulation is running.
steps.caption: English teaching image adapted from KIDSPRO’s screenshot. Click to enlarge.

steps.title: Press 1 to pitch
steps.goal: Release the ball and get the bat ready.
actions: Click inside the simulation so it receives your keyboard input.
Press 1 on your keyboard.
Watch the ramp tilt and the bat move to 180°.
steps.check: The ball rolls towards the bat.
steps.caption: English teaching image adapted from KIDSPRO’s screenshot. Click to enlarge.

steps.title: Press 2 to hit
steps.goal: Timing matters!
actions: When the ball reaches the bat, press 2.
Watch the bat swing back to 0°.
Reset before the next try. Try pressing 2 a little earlier or later.
steps.check: The bat moves. Can you time it to hit the ball?
steps.caption: English teaching image adapted from KIDSPRO’s screenshot. Click to enlarge.

steps.title: Try a sliding stopper
steps.goal: Optional route: release the ball with a slider instead of tilting the ramp.
actions: Use a separate copy for this alternative. Start from the author’s slider example if you need the shapes.
Set the ramp at an angle. Put a stopper in place to hold the ball.
Add a Slider Connector and connect one Joint Point to the stopper. Leave the other point unattached.
Point the slider along the stopper’s upward path, as shown.
steps.check: The stopper can slide upward to release the ball.
steps.tip: Choose one launch mechanism for each game. In this alternative, the slider releases the ball; the bat still uses an Axis Connector.
steps.caption: English teaching image adapted from KIDSPRO’s screenshot. Click to enlarge.

steps.title: Set the slider motor
steps.goal: Keep the stopper still until a key changes its speed.
actions: Select the Slider Connector. Set Motor Type to Continuous.
Enter each value in the table below.
Check that Motor Speed starts at 0.
steps.check: The stopper stays still when the simulation first starts.
steps.caption: English teaching image adapted from KIDSPRO’s screenshot. Click to enlarge.

steps.title: Give key 1 a speed action
steps.goal: A speed command is different from a target-angle command.
actions: Click Edit Interaction and select key 1.
Choose Change Speed and enter 200 units/s.
Start the simulation. Press 1 to test the stopper’s upward movement.
steps.check: The action is Change Speed and the value is 200 units/s.
steps.caption: This image shows an intermediate state: the action menu still reads None. Complete the next action by choosing Change Speed and entering 200 units/s.

steps.title: Test the alternative launcher
steps.goal: Watch the stopper release the ball.
actions: Start from the reset position with the ball behind the stopper.
Start the simulation. Press 1 and watch the stopper move up.
If you are using the author’s baseball example, press 2 to swing the bat.
Reset before trying again. Compare this release with the tilting ramp.
steps.check: The stopper moves up and the ball rolls out.
steps.caption: Use the slider interaction from the previous step, then test it in Sim Lab.

vocab: A connector that lets a shape turn around an axis.
A connector that lets a shape move in a straight line.
The part of a connector you drag onto a shape to attach it.
A motor mode that moves to a target position or angle.
A motor mode that uses speed to control movement.
Move to an exact target angle, such as 22.5° or 180°.
The turning force of a motor.
Revolutions per minute: a unit for rotational speed.
troubles: The ramp turns the wrong way.
Reset and return to design mode. Check the Axis Connector’s 90° rotation and compare its direction with step 9.
Check steps 2–4. Tilt by 22.5°, raise the bottom to height 0, then return to horizontal without lowering it.
Check that a Joint Point is attached to the bat. Confirm Servo mode and the two Set Position actions: key 1 → 180°, key 2 → 0°.
That is expected in the ramp version. Key 1 tilts the ramp and prepares the bat. Key 2 swings the bat back to 0°.
Nothing happens when I press a key.
Start the simulation first. Click in the Tinkercad simulation, then press the key. Make sure you are not typing into a settings box or this guide.
Reset. Check the ball’s path and the bat’s height. Then try pressing 2 earlier or later. Change one thing at a time.
The slider does not release the ball.
Check the connection and upward direction. Motor Speed starts at 0. Key 1 must use Change Speed with 200 units/s. Start the simulation before pressing the key.
The English image and my screen look different.
The images are adapted teaching illustrations from the source’s 2025 interface. Use the written settings for exact values. Your Tinkercad layout may differ.
